operations.description: Page through the audit log in sequence order. Filter by event kinds (for example egress.denied or command.denied) and outcome; pass the returned nextAfterSeq to continue. Inputs appear only as digests unless a capability allow-lists a field.

Recompute the audit log hash chain up to the current head and report any edited, removed, reordered or truncated events. A clean result proves internal consistency; compare the head with an off-host copy to rule out a full rewrite.

Read the current security posture: hardening profile, network mode, every declared destination with whether it is bound, disabled or isolated and how often it was used or denied, policy findings, audit-chain integrity and audit forwarding health. Use it to answer what this installation can reach and whether its audit trail is intact.
Read the scanner profiles and scan routes configured for one station. Stations use them to decode scanner input and map scans to intents without a model turn.
Replace the ordered scan routes of a station as its administrator. The first matching route wins; patterns are validated before they are stored.
Remove one scanner profile from a station as its administrator.

Create or replace one scanner profile at a station as its administrator. Use the calibration result from the setup screen; supply device:<station> in expectedRevisions to avoid overwriting a concurrent change.
List qualitative code groups and defect codes published by the quality system, with their valuation.
Set the usage decision for a fully inspected open lot as supervisor. Supply lot:<id> in expectedRevisions so results recorded after you reviewed the lot cause a conflict instead of being ignored.
Record a defect with a catalog code and quantity for an open lot as inspector or supervisor.
Integration principal only: record the quality system outcome for a forwarded result, defect or decision.

Read one inspection lot with its characteristics, specification limits, active results, defects, usage decision and the next open sample. Use its revision as lot:<id> in a decision expectedRevisions map.
List inspection lots at plants where you hold a role, with capture progress and synchronization counts. Authorization precedes filtering, counting and pagination.
Integration principal only: apply a batch of lots and code groups from the quality system and advance the watermark. A stale from watermark conflicts.

Summarize capture economics for your plants: datapoints captured by humans and by agents with median and 90th-percentile milliseconds from ready to commit, corrections, out-of-tolerance results, and how long the quality system took to accept forwarded records.
List plants where you hold a role. Supervisors also see the plant membership.
Grant or remove a plant role as supervisor of that plant. A null role removes access. You cannot change your own role. Permission changes invalidate affected views.

Supersede a result with a corrected value or code and a reason. Supervisors may correct any result at their plant; inspectors only their own. The original is retained for audit. Use this to resolve a quality-system rejection.

Record one measured value (quantitative) or code (qualitative) for a characteristic sample of an open lot as inspector or supervisor. occurredAt is when the measurement happened (epoch ms, at most 24 h old). Omit sample to use the next open one. The receipt proves the local commit; the quality system accepts or rejects it later.
Record up to 100 measurements for one open lot in a single commit, for example from an instrument export. All succeed or none do. Each result is forwarded to the quality system separately.
Summarize synchronization with the quality system for your plants: pending, accepted and rejected records, the oldest pending item, recent rejections and the last master-data sync.
Return the next characteristic and sample to measure for an open lot, and how many samples remain. Call it after each recorded result to drive capture.
List what needs a person at a station: readings the bridge could not read with confidence, and screen procedures that were interrupted and must be reconciled.
Set what the station bridge may do as supervisor: monitor-only (observe), assist (hazard-free procedures) or actuate (all declared procedures).
Station bridge only: read the bridge mode and who holds the station screen. The bridge reads this before every screen action.

Confirm the good and scrap counters the station shows for the active order and forward them to the MES. Uses only confident or operator-verified readings; pass counters:<id> (countersRevision from line.station.get) in expectedRevisions so counts that changed after you looked conflict instead of being sent.
Resolve an interrupted screen procedure as a person who checked the station: applied=true records it as done; applied=false lets the bridge run it again.
Integration only: record the outcome of a forwarded record (MES) or a screen procedure (station bridge). Each integration principal settles only its own target.
MES integration only: apply orders and stop reasons from the MES and advance the watermark. A stale from watermark conflicts.

Station bridge only: submit what the station screen currently shows. Stable confident readings become observed values, unsure ones become attention items, and machine state changes open and close stops.
List MES orders released to a station, and the active one, with material and recipe.

Start a released MES order at a station: records the desired recipe and asks the station bridge to load it through the station screen. Needs a person at the station (operator or supervisor, not an agent): the receipt proves the request, the station shows the result later. Starts only when the machine is stopped.
Confirm or correct a reading the bridge was unsure about, as a person at the station. The value becomes operator-verified and resolves the attention item.
List stop reasons published by the MES.
Take over the station screen from the bridge (seat=operator) or hand it back (seat=agent) as operator or supervisor. Taking over stops any running screen procedure before its next action.

Read one station: observed readings with source, confidence and freshness, the current order, desired versus observed recipe, the open stop and bridge state. Observed values come from the station screen and may be stale; check `stale` and `status` before relying on them. Pass countersRevision as counters:<id> in a count confirmation expectedRevisions map.
List stations where you hold a role with machine state, open stop, attention count, bridge mode and who holds the station screen.
Grant or remove a station role (operator, supervisor, viewer) as supervisor of that station. A null role removes access. You cannot change your own role or give integration principals a role.
Classify a detected machine stop with an MES stop reason as operator or supervisor. The classification is forwarded to the MES; a rejected classification can be classified again.
List machine stops detected at a station, newest first, with classification and MES synchronization status. Filter to open (unclassified) stops with `unclassified`.
Summarize synchronization for your stations: records pending, held, accepted and rejected per target (MES and station software), recent rejections and the last MES sync.
Archive a project as its owner. Tasks remain readable, but task edits are blocked until the project is restored. Supply project:<id> in expectedRevisions to detect concurrent edits.
Create a project as workspace owner. The creator becomes a project owner. Returns the project and its committed revision.
Read one accessible project and its current revision. The membership map is included only for project owners.
List accessible projects with optional archive filtering. Authorization is applied before pagination and the count includes only accessible matching projects.
Restore an archived project as its owner, permitting ordinary task edits again. Supply project:<id> in expectedRevisions to detect concurrent edits.

Set or remove a project membership as project owner. A null role removes access; workspace-owner membership is fixed. Permission changes invalidate affected views. Supply project:<id> in expectedRevisions.
Create a todo task in an accessible, active project as owner or editor. Only owners may supply privateNote. Returns the task and its committed revision.
Remove a task from an active project as owner or editor. This capability has no restore operation. Supply task:<id> in expectedRevisions to detect concurrent changes.
Read one accessible task and its current revision. privateNote is included only for project owners. Use this revision in a later mutation expectedRevisions map.

List tasks in accessible projects, with public-field search, status/project filters and pagination. Authorization precedes filtering and count calculation. privateNote is owner-only and cannot be searched or sorted.
Set a task to todo, doing or done in an active project as owner or editor. Supply task:<id> in expectedRevisions to detect concurrent changes.

Edit task title or description in an active project as owner or editor; privateNote is owner-only. Project reassignment is not accepted. Supply task:<id> in expectedRevisions to prevent overwriting a concurrent edit.

network.purpose: Forward audit events off the host (RFC 5424 syslog over TLS).
Serve the frontend, API, events and attach connections.
Forward stop classifications and count confirmations to the MES and pull orders and reasons.
Model catalog and inference for Codex and AI SDK runs.
ChatGPT sign-in: token exchange, OIDC discovery, signing keys and revocation.
Forward results, defects and usage decisions to the quality system and pull lots and characteristics from it.
Reach the legacy station software screen to observe it and run declared procedures (web HMI, VNC or RDP, per site).

processes.purpose: Claude Code process driven by the Agent SDK.
Codex app-server harness under a delegated grant.
Browser that reaches a web-based station HMI for the screen bridge.

workflows.text: Read the station configuration first. Save a scanner profile only from values the user confirmed or a calibration produced; never guess prefixes, suffixes or layouts. Keep specific scan routes before general ones and test a pattern against an example code the user supplies.

Find the unclassified stop, read the station state and alarm text at the stop and the MES stop reasons, and propose the reason that the alarm and history support, with your evidence. Classify only after the operator confirms the reason; never classify a stop from a guess. If no reason fits, say so.

Find the open lot, read its characteristics and limits, then record each measurement for the sample named by the worklist. For an instrument export, map rows to characteristics and samples and submit them with record-batch in one commit; never invent values that are not in the source. Use the measurement time from the source as occurredAt. Report out-of-tolerance results and record a defect only when the source states one. Leave the usage decision to a supervisor.
Create a project from the brief, add concrete tasks, inspect the scoped task list, and update each task status as work progresses.

Start with the posture. For any check that is not passing, list the matching audit events (for example kinds egress.denied, command.denied or posture.checked) and verify the chain before drawing conclusions. Report destinations by ID and state; never infer that an unbound destination was reached.

Summarize each station for the next shift: active order and counters with their freshness and source, stops and their classification, open attention items and held screen procedures, and records the MES rejected. Report observed values as observed (with time and confidence), not as facts.

Read rejected records from sync status, inspect the lot and the rejection reason, and explain each one. Correct a result only when the reason identifies a clear entry error and the correct value is known; supply that reason. Otherwise ask the user. A correction is forwarded again and may itself be rejected.
